title: OmniVia Chat Runtime Contract v1 - F2a provider-invocation projection
description: The F2a provider-invocation projection: a Chat-owned wire shape over one Provider Invocation (REF-019 §5.7) driving a Generation Attempt (generation.schema.json). F2a is a projection of the Chat Runtime Contract, not an independent public authority; it reuses REF-019 Provider Invocation and Boundary Result semantics by reference and never redefines Provider Service authority, and it originates its own closed event-discriminator, finish-reason and error-code vocabularies because REF-019 §18.8 and §7.9 leave the exact wire shape to a contract definition (REF-019 §7.1 Contract Ownership belongs to DOC-004). Provider credentials, arbitrary headers or URLs, raw request/response bodies, protected chain-of-thought content and SDK objects or exceptions are forbidden on this wire boundary; every field is either a stable identity, a closed vocabulary member, a bounded structured value, or an explicitly sanitised optional identity. `ProviderInvocationRequest` is the wire request; `ProviderEvent` (`stream-start` through `finish`/`error`) is the wire stream; `ProviderInvocationRecord` is the separate durable Core-owned record of truth Core persists to recover across retries and fallbacks (CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-CATALOGUE.json's `f2a.recordSchemaRef` names it as catalogue-reachable) — the three are related but never interchangeable. Exactly one terminal `finish` or `error` event is permitted per Attempt event stream; a stream that ends without one is `malformed-response` (CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-FREEZE.md §11). Repeated provider-issued tool IDs across distinct model steps are disambiguated by `attemptId` plus `stepId` (technical delivery specification §12.7, trace class 3).

FinishReason.title: FinishReason
FinishReason.description: The closed v1 normalised finish-reason vocabulary (technical delivery specification §12.7), conceptually aligned to REF-019 §18.8 by concept, not by shared schema, since REF-019 leaves the exact enum to contract definition.

ProviderErrorCode.title: ProviderErrorCode
ProviderErrorCode.description: The closed v1 stable provider error-code vocabulary (technical delivery specification §12.7), conceptually aligned to REF-019 §7.9 Stable Diagnostics by concept, not by shared schema. Never a raw upstream provider or SDK exception.

ProviderEventType.title: ProviderEventType
ProviderEventType.description: The closed v1 normalised provider event-discriminator vocabulary (technical delivery specification §12.7). Additive event types are a compatible minor extension; a strict decoder that receives an unrecognised type applies the additive-decode policy in CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-FREEZE.md §11 (safe diagnostic and resnapshot), never a guessed interpretation.

ToolChoice.title: ToolChoice
ToolChoice.description: Bounded tool-choice directive. `toolName` is present if and only if `mode` is `named`.

inputSchema.description: A Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema object for the tool's input shape.

ProviderMessagePart.title: ProviderMessagePart
ProviderMessagePart.description: One part of an outbound provider-facing message. Never a raw prompt string; always a typed, bounded structure. Each `kind` permits and requires only its own appropriate fields (freeze §11): `text` carries `text` only; `reasoning` carries no content field at all, because protected chain-of-thought is forbidden on this wire boundary (freeze §11 rule 5); `tool-call` carries `toolCallId`, `toolName` and `input`; `tool-result` carries `toolCallId` and `output`; `file` carries `attachmentReference`; `source` carries an `evidenceReference` or a non-empty `displayLabel` (or both), mirroring `SourceEvent`. `input`/`output` are semantically opaque tool payloads, bounded here to at most 1024 top-level properties each; this schema does not by itself prove a total byte or nesting-depth ceiling, and relies on F2a's own frozen 16 MiB (16,777,216-byte) maximum serialized request/event size (CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-FREEZE.md §15, matching the existing `bridge.schema.json#/$defs/ContextBoundMessage.maxMessageBytes` ceiling F2b already freezes) for the total size bound.

schemaRef.description: Required if and only if `kind` is `structured`; an opaque reference to the requested output schema, never the inline schema body.

GenerationOptions.title: GenerationOptions
GenerationOptions.description: Bounded, closed generation-tuning options. Every field is optional; omission means the adapter's own default applies.

SanitisedScalarValue.title: SanitisedScalarValue
SanitisedScalarValue.description: One bounded scalar value permitted inside an intentionally extensible F2a provider-options or provider-metadata map. Deliberately excludes nested object values so this shape alone cannot smuggle an arbitrarily deep or large structure. The `number` branch is itself finitely bounded (±1,000,000,000), matching the intent of every other numeric bound in this bundle -- a provider-options or provider-metadata value that is genuinely a bounded tuning knob or count never needs a magnitude past this ceiling. This is not by itself proof the value is free of a credential, header or URL: a scalar string can still carry any text. `BoundedExtensiblePropertyName`'s reserved-key denylist and the installed adapter's own closed option schema are the actual defences; see §15 in CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-FREEZE.md.

BoundedExtensiblePropertyName.title: BoundedExtensiblePropertyName
BoundedExtensiblePropertyName.description: A bounded property name for an intentionally extensible F2a provider-options or provider-metadata map. Rejects the common reserved names under which a credential, header, URL or endpoint value is most likely to be smuggled, matched case-insensitively via an explicit per-letter case class (never a Python-only inline flag group), so this pattern compiles and behaves identically under `new RegExp(...)` in an ECMA-262 (JavaScript/Ajv) consumer as it does here. This is a defence-in-depth denylist, not proof that every possible secret-shaped value is caught by this shape alone; the installed adapter's own closed option schema remains the actual runtime authority (§15).

ProviderOptionNamespace.title: ProviderOptionNamespace
ProviderOptionNamespace.description: The exact provider or adapter family a namespaced provider-options value applies to.

ProviderOptionsNamespaceValue.title: ProviderOptionsNamespaceValue
ProviderOptionsNamespaceValue.description: One namespace's bounded provider-options object (REF-019 §5.2 leaves adapter-specific knobs to contract definition). Every value is a bounded scalar or an array of bounded scalars, never a nested object. Provider options remain adapter-schema validated at runtime; an opaque namespace object satisfying this shape alone is not proof of credential/header/URL safety (§15).

ProviderOptionsByNamespace.title: ProviderOptionsByNamespace
ProviderOptionsByNamespace.description: Bounded, provider-namespaced tuning options that do not fit `GenerationOptions` (REF-019 §5.2 leaves adapter-specific knobs to contract definition), keyed by the exact provider or adapter family each value applies to. An actual bounded map, not one anonymous `{namespace, options}` object, so more than one adapter family's options can be carried on a single request. Never a credential, raw header, raw URL or SDK object; each namespace's value remains subject to the installed adapter's own closed option schema at runtime (§15).

ReconciliationState.title: ReconciliationState
ReconciliationState.description: The closed v1 vocabulary for whether a terminal or indeterminate Provider Invocation Evidence record (`RouteEvidence`, `ProviderInvocationRecord`) has been reconciled against upstream provider truth.

ProviderInvocationRequest.title: ProviderInvocationRequest
ProviderInvocationRequest.description: The F2a request/admission projection, reconciled to the exact package-neutral request vocabulary the technical delivery specification §10 freezes: `invocationId, workspaceId, jobId, attemptId, connectionId, modelId, operation, messages[], tools[]?, toolChoice?, responseFormat?, generationOptions?, providerOptionsByNamespace?, deadlineAt?, classificationRef, residencyRef, idempotencyKey, correlationId`. `connectionId` and `modelId` name an already-resolved Provider route (REF-019 §5.5-§5.6); this record never carries credentials, raw endpoint URLs or arbitrary headers (REF-019 §6.12 No Generic Prompt Endpoint). `operation` is fixed to `language.stream`, the accepted W3 launch packet's streamed provider-invocation operation; no other operation is defined in this Review Candidate. `policyRef` is a W3 launch-packet addition, not part of the base technical-spec vocabulary. This Review Candidate's sole request shape is scoped to the accepted W3 Gate-B launch boundary, so `policyRef`, `classificationRef`, `residencyRef` and `deadlineAt` are all required here even though the base technical delivery specification marks `deadlineAt` generically optional (`deadlineAt?`) for the package-neutral vocabulary at large; this intentionally tightens that generic optional deadline for the commissioned Gate-B boundary, per the W3 launch packet §§1-3.

attemptId.description: The Chat Generation Attempt this request is driving. Distinct from a stream event's own `attemptId`, which references `ProviderAttemptId` (a transport-level Attempt); the record context makes the distinction explicit.

operation.description: Fixed to `language.stream`, matching the accepted W3 launch packet: this invocation uses the streamed provider event form (REF-019 §6.2 Invoke Streaming Provider).

policyRef.description: Opaque reference to the governing Provider policy (REF-019 §5.2); a W3 launch-packet addition required for the Gate-B launch boundary.

ConfiguredRoutePreference.title: ConfiguredRoutePreference
ConfiguredRoutePreference.description: The Provider route configured as this invocation's preference before it ran (REF-019 §5.5-§5.6): a named connection and model identity, never a raw endpoint URL or credential.

AdmittedProviderRoute.title: AdmittedProviderRoute
AdmittedProviderRoute.description: The concrete, admitted connection/model/adapter route this attempt actually ran against, distinct from `ConfiguredRoutePreference` whenever a same-route retry or an authorised fallback substituted a route (REF-019 §5.9).

RouteEvidence.title: RouteEvidence
RouteEvidence.description: Configured preference plus the concrete admitted connection/model/adapter route, decision, retry, timing, usage/cost and reconciliation Evidence, required whenever fallback selected a route other than the one configured (REF-019 §5.9 Fallback; F2a canonical trace classes 10-11). Every field this record requires is required whenever the record itself is present; a terminal event or `ProviderInvocationRecord` carrying `routeEvidence` at all therefore always carries complete route, timing and usage Evidence, never a partial one. `routeDecision`, `fallbackAuthorised`, `configuredPreference` and `admittedRoute` are relationally consistent: `fallback` requires `fallbackAuthorised: true` and an `admittedRoute` that differs from `configuredPreference`; `configured` and `same_route_retry` require `fallbackAuthorised: false` and an `admittedRoute` that does not differ from `configuredPreference`. JSON Schema alone cannot compare two nested sibling objects for equality, so this invariant is proven by the validator's `route_evidence_internally_consistent` relational check, not by a schema keyword.

fallbackAuthorised.description: True only for an explicit, authorised fallback to a route other than `configuredPreference` (REF-019 §5.9); never true for an undeclared, silent route substitution.

UsageCounts.title: UsageCounts
UsageCounts.description: Bounded token-usage counts by category (technical delivery specification §12.7-§12.8). Every field is optional, but at least one category is required; a category absent from the provider's own reporting is simply omitted, never guessed as zero, and an empty `UsageCounts` object carries no information and is rejected.

ProviderUsage.title: ProviderUsage
ProviderUsage.description: Usage broken out by provenance: `reported` is exactly what the provider itself returned; `estimated` is an OmniVia-computed approximation used when the provider under-reports or omits a category. The two are never merged into one unlabelled count. At least one of `reported` or `estimated` is required; an empty `ProviderUsage` object carries no information and is rejected.

EstimatedCost.title: EstimatedCost
EstimatedCost.description: A bounded, reproducible estimated-cost projection over `ProviderUsage`, never a provider-issued invoice.

TextLifecycleEvent.title: TextLifecycleEvent
TextLifecycleEvent.description: Covers `text-start`, `text-delta` and `text-end`. `delta` is present if and only if `eventType` is `text-delta`.

ReasoningLifecycleEvent.title: ReasoningLifecycleEvent
ReasoningLifecycleEvent.description: Covers `reasoning-start`, `reasoning-delta` and `reasoning-end`. Deliberately carries no reasoning content field: protected chain-of-thought is forbidden on this wire boundary (REF-042 §7.3 hidden reasoning is never a user-visible Message Part). Lifecycle presence only.

ToolInputLifecycleEvent.title: ToolInputLifecycleEvent
ToolInputLifecycleEvent.description: Covers `tool-input-start`, `tool-input-delta` and `tool-input-end`. `toolName` is present only on `tool-input-start`; `inputDelta` only on `tool-input-delta`; `input` only on `tool-input-end`.

FileEvent.title: FileEvent
FileEvent.description: Never raw bytes; identity only (CGAP-042-010 attachment semantics reused).

SourceEvent.title: SourceEvent
SourceEvent.description: A citation source. Never an arbitrary raw URL; an opaque reference or a bounded display label only.

ProviderMetadataEvent.title: ProviderMetadataEvent
ProviderMetadataEvent.description: Bounded provider metadata only, with property names and scalar values bounded via the same reusable `BoundedExtensiblePropertyName`/`SanitisedScalarValue` defs `ProviderOptionsByNamespace` uses. Never an SDK object, exception or raw response body. This bounding is defence-in-depth, not proof the metadata is free of every possible credential/header/URL-shaped value; see §15.

SanitisedResponseMetadata.title: SanitisedResponseMetadata
SanitisedResponseMetadata.description: Closed, sanitised response metadata sufficient for a stable provider response/model/time identity. Never an SDK object, exception, raw header, raw URL or raw response body; a value outside this shape is dropped by the adapter before this event is constructed, not passed through opaquely. `respondedAt` is always required, even when the provider itself supplies no response ID, model identity or system fingerprint: it is always locally knowable (Core stamps it when the terminal event is received), so an empty `{}` object can never satisfy this record.

providerModelId.description: The concrete model identity the provider itself reported serving the response, when it may differ from the requested `modelId`.

FinishCancellationState.title: FinishCancellationState
FinishCancellationState.description: Explicit, closed cancellation state carried on every `FinishEvent`, so a consumer never has to infer cancellation from `finishReason` alone.

FinishEvent.title: FinishEvent
FinishEvent.description: One of the two possible terminal event types (CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-FREEZE.md §11). `routeEvidence` is required whenever a fallback route differs from the configured route (trace class 11). `usage`, `responseMetadata` and `cancellationState` are required on every `FinishEvent`. Cancellation consistency: `finishReason: cancelled` requires `cancellationState: cancelled` and a bounded `cancellationInitiator`; every other `finishReason` requires `cancellationState: not_cancelled` and forbids `cancellationInitiator`.

cancellationInitiator.description: Required if and only if `cancellationState` is `cancelled`; states who or what initiated the cancellation.

ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent
ErrorEvent.description: The other possible terminal event type (CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-FREEZE.md §11). `retryable` and a sanitised `statusClass` are required on every `ErrorEvent`; provider request identity and `retryAfterSeconds` remain optional and bounded, since upstream does not always supply them.

statusClass.description: A sanitised, coarse status classification. Never a raw upstream HTTP status code or provider-specific status string.

ProviderInvocationLifecycleState.title: ProviderInvocationLifecycleState
ProviderInvocationLifecycleState.description: The closed v1 durable lifecycle vocabulary for one `ProviderInvocationRecord`, aligned by concept (not by shared schema) to REF-019 Appendix B's Invocation state model; this record never redefines Provider Service authority over that state model. `indeterminate` names a durable invocation whose outcome Core could not yet safely resolve (for example a crash between admission and a terminal transport event) and that requires reconciliation before it is treated as either succeeded or failed.

ProviderInvocationRecord.title: ProviderInvocationRecord
ProviderInvocationRecord.description: The durable, Core-owned record of truth for one logical Provider Invocation (REF-019 §5.7, §22.8-§22.11), distinct from and outliving any one transport Attempt (`ProviderAttemptId`) beneath it. Core persists exactly this shape to recover safely after a crash, a same-route retry, or an authorised fallback; it is never itself the wire request or a stream event, and it never claims to redefine Provider Service authority over Invocation identity or lifecycle. `attemptIds` lists every transport Attempt admitted under this invocation so far, oldest first, and is closed to duplicates (`uniqueItems`): the same transport Attempt is never listed twice. A non-terminal `lifecycleState` (`requested`, `in_progress`) carries neither `terminalAt` nor `routeEvidence`, so it never pretends a result already exists. A newly `requested` invocation may have zero Attempts (none has been admitted yet); every other lifecycle state (`in_progress`, and every terminal or indeterminate state) requires at least one, since each has already admitted at least one transport Attempt. A terminal `lifecycleState` (`succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`) requires both `terminalAt` and a complete `routeEvidence`, so Core can resume or reconcile safely from the record alone. `indeterminate` requires `reconciliationState` and forbids `routeEvidence`, since an indeterminate invocation has, by definition, no confirmed terminal route/result Evidence yet.

generationAttemptId.description: The Chat Generation Attempt this Provider Invocation is driving; distinct from a transport-level `ProviderAttemptId` (`attemptIds`).

connectionId.description: The requested named-connection identity, as admitted at invocation creation time. The concrete admitted route actually used (which may differ under retry or fallback) is `routeEvidence.admittedRoute`.

modelId.description: The requested model identity, as admitted at invocation creation time.

allOf.description: Only a newly `requested` invocation may have zero Attempts; every other lifecycle state has already admitted at least one.

ProviderEvent.title: ProviderEvent
ProviderEvent.description: The discriminated union of every F2a event $def, keyed by `eventType` (technical delivery specification §12.7). One trace fixture is an ordered sequence of `ProviderEvent` records, grouped by `(invocationId, attemptId)`.
